24.text: OMENS. — In the course of the preceding pages I have mentioned several

25.text: times the Chukchee belief in omens; for instance, should a slaughtered reindeer

26.text: fall upon the wound, this is considered as less favorable than to fall on the

27.text: opposite side, especially if the reindeer had been slaughtered for a definite

28.text: sacrifice. For the animal to fall backward forebodes misfortune. Therefore,

29.text: in the very process of slaughtering, the people try by dexterous jerking of the

30.text: halter to make the reindeer fall with the wound upward. It is not good,

31.text: however, to exaggerate this tendency, otherwise the sacrifice will not count

32.text: in the eyes of the divinities.

33.text: To dream of the loss of a tooth may presage illness or death, the tooth

34.text: symbolizing the soul, which is in danger of being lost. The yawning of

35.text: reindeer during a journey bodes the coming of evil spirits. The crackling of

36.text: the fire on the hearth foretells the coming of guests. The last sign, as is

37.text: well known, is widespread among various peoples.

38.text: TABOOS. — I did not find many taboos among the Chukchee, Reindeer

39.text: or Maritime, nor among the Asiatic Eskimo. In this, these tribes differ

40.text: greatly from the American Eskimo, whose whole life and whose pursuits

41.text: are closely interwoven with numerous taboos.
